name: Lamorinda Jewish Preschool
summary: A warm, play-based Jewish preschool in Lafayette, inspired by Reggio Emilia, where every child feels at home.
schedule: Monday to Thursday 8:30 AM – 5:00 PM; Friday 8:00 AM – 3:00 PM
details:
Two classes: **12 to 24 months** and **2 to 4 years**. Children learn through hands-on exploration, guided by Jewish values: kindness, respect, compassion, confidence and responsibility. We follow the principle *Chanoch L'naar Al Pi Darko*: teach each child in their own way.

## Tuition
- $17,000 for the school year, or 10 monthly payments of $1,700
- Includes daily lunch, books, supplies and enrichment
- Drop-in care: $22 per hour, when space allows
- Need-based scholarships are available

## Our team
- **Tzipora Labkowski**, Director: Master's in Education, more than 10 years in education
- **Rivka Burnstein**, 12–24 months class
- **Rivka Yegorova**, 2–4 years class

Enrollment for 2026–2027 is open. Schedule a tour: call 925-384-7242.

name: Lamorinda Hebrew School
summary: Hands-on, fun Jewish learning once a week, Sundays for two hours. Open to all, no membership required.
details:
## Three tracks
- **[Early Childhood (ages 3–5)](#early-childhood-ages-3-5):** stories, songs, crafts and holiday celebrations
- **[Hebrew School (ages 5–12)](#hebrew-school-ages-5-12):** Hebrew reading with Aleph Champ, holidays, traditions and Jewish pride
- **[Bar/Bat Mitzvah (ages 12–13)](#bar-bat-mitzvah-ages-12-13):** personal preparation for the big day

## Early Childhood (ages 3–5)
The youngest children discover being Jewish through stories, songs, crafts and holiday celebrations. They meet the first Hebrew letters, bake and taste the holidays, and feel Shabbat come alive. Lessons are hands-on and gentle, so every child feels at home from the first Sunday.

## Hebrew School (ages 5–12)
Children learn to read Hebrew with **Aleph Champ**, a level-by-level program: each child moves up at their own pace and celebrates every new level. Lessons use stories, games and creative projects, and cover prayer and the siddur, the weekly Torah portion, Israel, Jewish history, Shabbat and the holidays from Rosh Hashanah to Shavuot, and Jewish values and mitzvahs.

## Bar/Bat Mitzvah (ages 12–13)
Each child prepares personally with the Rabbi and Rebbetzin, at their own pace. Boys learn to read from the Torah and to put on tefillin; girls join the Bat Mitzvah Club. It is simple and stress-free for the family. See [Bar & Bat Mitzvah](/programs/bar-bat-mitzvah).

## How we care for every child
Rebbetzin Tzipora Labkowski directs the school and knows every family. Anything you share when you register, a learning need, an allergy or a medical note, is kept confidential and given to your child's teacher, so your child is safe, understood and helped. Children learn at their own pace, every child is welcome, and no child is ever turned away for lack of funds. You can call the Rebbetzin any time at 925-384-7241.

## Tuition
$600 per child, including books and supplies. A payment plan is available. No child will be turned away for lack of funds.

## Teachers
Rabbi Yisroel Labkowski, Rebbetzin Tzipora Labkowski, Morah Shira Gold and Morah Rachel Schwartz.

name: CKids Lamorinda Afterschool
summary: Afterschool with homework help, sports, STEAM, Hebrew and Jewish heritage activities, plus a hot meal.
details: Homework help, daily sports and STEAM, modern Hebrew, weekly specials (drama, dance, karate, Shabbat sing), holiday cooking, storytelling, field trips, snacks and lunch or dinner.

name: Lamorinda Jewish Summer Camp
summary: Seven weeks of Jewish songs, Shabbat parties, water play, art and friendship.
details:
Jewish songs and movement, Shabbat celebrations, water play, arts and crafts, sensory play, Hebrew and traditions, mitzvahs and kindness.

$3,200 for the full summer or $500 per week. Spaces are limited; early registration is recommended.

name: Torah Classes for Adults
summary: Weekly Torah, Tanya and Hebrew classes, one-on-one study and lively discussion. Questions welcome.
schedule: Sunday 9 PM (English Torah), Monday 8:30 PM (Tanya in Hebrew, with the Rebbetzin), Tuesday 8:30 PM (Hebrew, with a meal), Wednesday 1 PM (Tanya)
details: Learn at your own pace, from your very first class to deep Talmud and Kabbalah. Classes include the weekly Torah portion, Tanya (Chassidic philosophy), Explore the Talmud and practical Jewish living. Prefer to learn one-on-one? Ask the Rabbi to set up a study partner.

name: Jewish Women's Circle
summary: Creative evenings, challah bakes, workshops and inspiration with friends.
details: Past evenings include the Mega Challah Bake, Sip & Paint, Latkes & Latte, a ceramic Seder plate workshop and a pre-Shavuot cheese board workshop. Join the list to hear about the next one.

name: Men's Club
summary: Bagels, Lox & Tefillin, Scotch & Steaks in the Sukkah, and good company.
details: Fellowship, learning and a l'chaim. Ask about putting on tefillin or getting your own pair.

name: Kids & Teen Events
summary: Challah and matzah bakes, Havdalah glow parties, Krav Maga for teens, the Rabbi's Kitchen and more.
details: Favorites include the Model Matzah Bakery, Kids Hamantashen Bake, Havdalah Glow Party, Make Your Own Menorah, Sushi in the Sukkah, Mezuzah 4 U, Krav Maga for Teens and the Rabbi's Kitchen for teens.

name: Bar & Bat Mitzvah
summary: Personal, simple preparation at your child's pace, with hands-on learning and a Bat Mitzvah Club. Every family is welcome.
details: It is straightforward: we guide you step by step and take care of the details. No Hebrew or background is needed, there is no membership, and every Jewish family is welcome, whatever your background or budget. Every child learns at their own pace with the Rabbi and Rebbetzin. Boys learn to read from the Torah and put on tefillin; girls join the Bat Mitzvah Club. Find the date with our [Bar/Bat Mitzvah calculator](/tools/bar-bat-mitzvah), read [Bar and Bat Mitzvah made simple](/learn/bar-bat-mitzvah-made-simple), and call the Rabbi at 925-384-7242 to begin.

name: Bay Kosher
summary: Kosher meat, groceries and Judaica in Lafayette: shop online for pickup or delivery across the Bay Area.
details:
**Bay Kosher is part of Chabad of Lamorinda.** It is a nonprofit kosher market in the Chabad building at 3477 Golden Gate Way, Lafayette, behind the Lafayette Library, built with the gifts of this community so that keeping kosher in Lafayette, Moraga, Orinda and the whole East Bay is easy.

**What you can get:** kosher meat and poultry, deli and prepared foods, baked goods and challah, dairy, frozen foods, groceries, candy and snacks, drinks, household items, and Judaica (Shabbat candles, menorahs, mezuzahs and more), with holiday foods for every Jewish holiday.

**How it works:** order online at [shop.baykosher.com](https://shop.baykosher.com) (in English, Hebrew or Russian) and pick up at the store, usually in about 3 hours, or have it delivered across the Bay Area. You can also come in and shop.

**Store hours:** Sunday 11 AM to 4 PM, Monday to Thursday 10 AM to 6 PM, Friday 10 AM to 2:30 PM. Store phone: (925) 440-1226.

**A short history:** in 2020 Chabad of Lamorinda began selling kosher meat at the center, when almost none could be bought in Contra Costa County. In December 2021 Chabad bought its own building, and in 2022 Bay Kosher opened inside it.

Need something special, a kosher order for a simcha, or help keeping kosher? Call the Rabbi at 925-384-7242. See also [kosher in Lamorinda](/learn/kosher-in-lamorinda).

name: Chai Club
summary: No dues, no building fund: our community is carried by monthly partners giving in multiples of 18.
details: Chabad of Lamorinda has no membership dues. The Chai Club partners make it all possible with a monthly gift in multiples of 18 ($18, $36, $72, $180, $360 and up). Give Chai, get Chai! See the [Chai Club honor board](/chai-club#partners).
